## C4.1 Intergenerational Justice

C4.1 is class M with two clauses: general government gross debt below 80% of GDP, and positive net national saving (gross savings less consumption of fixed capital, % of GNI) over the scoring window. The four configured economies and the four Nordic countries are read on the IMF's and the World Bank's series (cached in `evidence_cache/C4.1/`). The capital-consumption series ends in 2021, so the window is 2015-2021; debt is the 2024 figure, the last complete year. **Qatar rises from 0.5 to 1.0** (both clauses cleared; flagged toward 0.5 because the measure does not net resource depletion). **Status Quo rises from 0.0 to 0.5** (a correction: its published 0.0 rested on carbon and ecology, which C4.2 now holds; net saving is positive). China, Singapore and Nordic Social Democracy hold at 0.5, each short on clause 1 only (Singapore and Nordic Social Democracy flagged toward 1.0). The ten designs and mechanisms are held at their published scores, none of whose sources states a debt path or a saving path; Libertarian Minarchism and Stakeholder Capitalism stay at 0.0 on protocol 2.1's first condition. Anyone who can supply a design's own debt or saving path can challenge its unit through the site's contribution route.

## C4.4 Power Distribution

C4.4 is class M with two clauses: democratic accountability for at least 80% of major decisions (the share of employment in organizations whose decisions are taken or elected by those they affect, public bodies counting only where V-Dem's Regimes of the World makes the country a democracy) and functional removal and replacement mechanisms. The four configured economies are read on V-Dem's classification (cached in `evidence_cache/C4.4/`): the United States is a liberal democracy (clause 2 cleared, clause 1 short on any count); China and Qatar are closed autocracies and Singapore an electoral autocracy (both clauses short). **Status Quo rises from 0.0 to 0.5**: its published 0.0 rested on wealth concentration, which v2.0 measures once, in C1.2b. China, Singapore and Qatar hold at 0.0; Singapore is flagged toward 0.5. The twelve designs and mechanisms are held at their published scores: none of their sources states a share of workers in accountable organizations or a removal mechanism, and each 0.0 rests on protocol 2.1's first or third condition. Anyone who can supply such a share or mechanism for a design can challenge its unit through the site's contribution route.

## C3.4 Epistemic Adaptability

C3.4 is class M with four clauses: parameter adjustability of at least 30%, policy updates within six months of evidence, changes open to challenge and reversal by those affected, and no collapse during adjustment. Seven units were not yet re-estimated. **Integral falls from 1.0 to 0.5**, a correction on the precedent of part (b1): its adjustment cycle is shown in the white paper's own illustration, which projects rather than observes, so clauses 1, 2 and 4 are not shown; the unit is flagged toward 1.0 for the design's deliberation loop. **Integral's total falls from 14.5 to 14.0, so first place is no longer shared with CCO-PTF-CIP-SZH unless another unit moves.** Status Quo, China and Qatar hold at 0.5; Centrally Planned Socialism and Libertarian Minarchism hold at 0.0; Fully Automated Luxury Communism holds at 0.5. No figure is recomputed here: the readings rest on dated public events and on the published rationales.

## C4.5 Exploitation Elimination

C4.5 is class D: v2.0 deleted the clause on the share of decisions made under duress (measured once, in C2.1), so a unit keeps or raises its score. Seventeen units were not yet re-estimated and are read on the two remaining clauses: extraction rates below 10% of GDP, and genuine exit rights from exploitative relationships. No unit shows clause 2, so none is 1.0. **Participatory Economics rises from 0.0 to 0.5**: the design removes the three extraction relationships (clause 1 cleared), and its published 0.0 rested on coordination burdens and informal hierarchy, the residual-coercion reading v2.0 deleted. **This puts it level with CCO-PTF-CIP-SZH at 14.5 for first place**, and it is flagged toward 0.0. The other sixteen hold; the seven 0.0s rest on structural extraction (Status Quo, China, Singapore, Qatar) or on no structural connection to the three relationships (Doughnut Economics, Sovereign Wealth Fund Statism).

## C2.5 Exit Rights and Mobility

C2.5 is class D: v2.0 deleted the fourth clause (voluntary association, now measured once in C2.6), so a unit keeps or raises its score, and a 0.5 whose only unshown clause was association rises. Thirteen units were not yet re-estimated. The published rationale of each of the eight 0.5s was read for that clause and none rests on it (each names exit, differential treatment or mobility), so **nothing rises: all 13 hold**. The five 0.0s (Nordic Social Democracy, Market Socialism, Universal Basic Income, Degrowth, Fully Automated Luxury Communism) rest on the published finding that the system cannot function with large-scale opt-out, a whole-criterion reason that the deleted clause does not touch. Anyone who can show a unit's exit terms differ from its published rationale can challenge the unit through the site's contribution route.

## C1.1 Poverty Elimination Capacity

C1.1 is class I with two clauses: at least 90% poverty reduction within 20 years, and at least 85% under stress, where poverty is the World Bank Societal Poverty Line headcount (2021 PPP) and reduction is (baseline - rate at year 20) / baseline. The Platform's headcount (cached in `evidence_cache/C1.1/`) gives the configured economies' figures: the United States 19.0% in 2004 and 20.2% in 2024 (no reduction), China 47.8% in 2002 and 19.7% in 2022 (a reduction of 58.8%), Qatar one observation (17.6% in 2017), Singapore none. **Nothing moves: all 14 units hold**, none at 1.0. Status Quo stays at 0.5 because the 0.0 band requires the absence of any state mechanism; China's 58.8% sits inside the 0.5 band; Singapore and Qatar cannot be computed. The nine designs and mechanisms are held at their published scores because none states a projected rate at the Societal Poverty Line; Libertarian Minarchism stays at 0.0 on protocol 2.1's second condition. The Nordic countries' headcount at the same line has risen since 2000 (Sweden 7.3% to 12.4%), which bears on Nordic Social Democracy's earlier reading, not on this group's units; it is noted for the owner.

## C2.1 Freedom from Coercion

C2.1 is class I with two clauses: at least 70% of adults reporting genuine autonomy (Gallup World Poll, 'freedom to make life choices'), and revealed-preference evidence. The Gallup series could not be fetched in this session (the World Happiness Report's file is blocked from the container and no open republication was found), so the indicator is not re-measured. **All 15 units hold at their published scores, and the verdict cannot move on that series:** clause 2 is aspirational and no unit names a study, so none can be 1.0; the five 0.0s (Centrally Planned Socialism, Libertarian Minarchism, Doughnut Economics, China, Qatar) rest on whole-criterion findings. Re-measuring the four configured economies on the Gallup share is an open item that cannot change a verdict under the rule above.

## C2.4 Democratic Participation

C2.4 is class I with three clauses: turnout of at least 70% of the voting-age population, at least 35% of citizen proposals adopted, and at least 65% saying the system lets people like them have a say. **All 15 units hold at their published scores.** No unit in play shows clause 2: the configured economies have no binding citizen-initiative process at the national level (v2.0: where none exists the clause is not met) and the designs state no adoption rate, so none can be 1.0; the four 0.0s (Centrally Planned Socialism, Fully Automated Luxury Communism, China, Qatar) rest on the absence of any participation mechanism. The IDEA turnout series and the OECD trust survey were not re-fetched; re-measuring them is an open item that cannot change a verdict under the rule above.

## C2.3 Creative Development Opportunities

C2.3 is class I with three clauses: 50% regular creative engagement (aspirational unless a survey recording weekly frequency is named), 10 or more weekly hours on non-subsistence pursuits, and purpose scores of at least 70/100. **All 15 units hold at their published scores.** No unit in play names a survey for clause 1, so none can be 1.0; the lone 0.0 (Centrally Planned Socialism) rests on the suppression of creative expression. The time-use and well-being series were not re-fetched; re-measuring them is an open item that cannot change a verdict under the rule above.
